reviewer: The sceptic of AI in games
quit_moment: About minute 9.5 to 10: Ron Kirby had closed two separate chats with the same line, 'Right, boss. I'd best watch the rank.'
most_exciting_moment: Minute 9.5 to 9.6: fronting up to Darren over the debt, with the stare, threat and shove in front of a witness.
top_praise: The scripted openers are properly written: Sheila Dunn listing the debts and Ron Kirby pitching the ferry job sound like people with a past.
top_complaint: Free conversation falls back on the same evasive stock exits, so it reads like a machine that has run out of things to say, and the game announces that machine up front.
evidence: Ron closing two chats with the identical 'Right, boss. I'd best watch the rank.' and Sheila with 'That's all I have for you. The book's waiting.'
text: The game told me up front that anything I say freely is answered by an AI. The set-piece writing is good. Then I tried talking for myself and it fell apart. Ron ended two different chats with the exact same line, 'I'd best watch the rank'. Sheila kept telling me 'the book's waiting'. Asking anyone anything just gets a polite brush-off. Ten minutes in I could see the pattern and I was done. If I'm paying full price for handmade 1990s Britain, I don't want a chatbot in a flat cap. Thumbs down.
